examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Divide-and-conquer needs smaller subproblems, a base case and a correct combine procedure. The combine invariant uses assumed correctness of recursive results. Logarithmic depth does not imply logarithmic work because every branch counts. Overlapping subproblems may benefit from memoization, changing the algorithm's work model. For sorting/counting combinations, distinguish costs spent splitting, solving and merging.

**Key relationship:** T(n)=sum of recursive costs + divide/combine work

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Identify decreasing size.
2. Prove combine correctness.
3. Count all nodes or level work.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Identify independent subproblems, a shrinking parameter and combine cost. Prove a combine invariant using correctness of smaller subproblems. Logarithmic depth does not imply logarithmic total work: all subproblems at every level count. Memoization changes work when subproblems overlap.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A recurrence creates four size-n/2 children per node and stops at size 1. For n=8, how many leaves occur?

**Answer: 64.** There are log₂8=3 splitting levels. Four-way branching gives 4³=64 leaves, equal to n². The depth is only three but the leaf count is quadratic.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Overlapping recursion can repeat work exponentially. A recurrence for the return value may differ from the recurrence for runtime.

Splitting into halves does not automatically imply logarithmic total time; all recursive branches contribute.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Merging two sorted lists of total length n has time:

- **A.** Θ(n)
- **B.** Θ(n²)
- **C.** Θ(1)
- **D.** Θ(log n)

**Answer: A.** Each output element is emitted once while pointers advance through both lists; worst-case work is linear.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Independent subproblems can be combined
- **B.** Logarithmic depth always means logarithmic total work
- **C.** Base cases must be reachable
- **D.** Repeated overlapping subproblems can cause redundant work

**Answer: A, C, D.** Branching and local work can make total work much larger than depth.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Each node has three children of half the size until size 1. Starting at n=8, how many leaves?



**Answer: 27.** There are log₂8=3 splitting levels. Leaf count is 3³=27.
